name: Joe McCoul
role: Medora cowman and 1885 fall round-up foreman
bio: Joe McCoul was a Medora cowman who won a bronco in a raffle in December 1884 and in April 1885 bought cow horses at Miles City with Howard Eaton. In June 1885 he broke his leg when a bronco ran away with a load of posts at Van Eeghen's Garner Creek ranch, and he went to Glendive for treatment before returning in late July. That September the Little Missouri River Stockgrowers' Association named him foreman of the fall round-up, and in April 1886 a motion that the association stand by him in a dispute with the Bad Lands Cattle Co. over an animal was declared lost. In July 1886 he returned from a western horse-buying trip, and his horse Blue Jay was barred from that month's pony race.
